results.transcript: The situation was, I was the PM on checkout at a grocery delivery app, which had 2,100,000 weekly orders at the time. The problem was cart abandonment had sat at 31% for three straight quarters, and it had been getting worse for nine months. Before that, I had already tried a couple of quick fixes myself, and neither one moved the number, so I knew this needed a real investigation, not another patch. So what I did was pull 14 session recordings, and I found mobile users hit a nine field address form right before payment. I built a proposal and I went to Priya, our design lead, with three specific options. I also walked Priya through exactly how each option would land differently for our highest value customers, since that was the group leadership cared about most. I decided to ship a single page flow behind a feature flag to 5% of users, and I wrote the rollout plan myself with two rollback triggers at fifteen minute intervals. I checked in with Priya twice a week during the rollout, so we could react fast if anything looked off. As a result, abandonment improved to 22% within six weeks, and we verified it across two regions. What I learned is to size the fix to the evidence I actually had, and I have used that rule three times since.
